short_description: Non-canonical FirstPersonEmbodiment prototype layered on the accepted CH9.6 character, clothing, Item Graph and ENet presentation stack.
purpose: Evaluate first-person hands, clothing-visible viewmodels, independent left/right grip UX and low-latency item-selection presentation without reopening or mutating the frozen CH9.6 checkpoint and without weakening authority over concrete item actions.
expected_outcome: A separate research lab can render two first-person hands, switch the local active hotbar slot without a durable Item Graph round-trip, project upper clothing into first person, exercise local-only grab targets, and keep concrete item mutations server-authoritative.
current_stage: FPE-R1 Fix8 — remove durable hotbar selection from the interactive main-thread path
progress_note: Operator evidence confirms Fix6 removed the continuous and once-per-second main-thread hitch and made Tab/inventory smooth. Fix7 fixed the stale item left in the hand when an empty slot is selected, but the operator still observes an approximately half-second total SceneTree freeze on every hotbar selection: movement, rendering and character simulation stop together during the switch. Code review identifies the root cause. CH9.6 starts Ch9PersistentEquipmentDedicatedServerRuntime and Ch9GraphicalClientRuntime as children of the same lab SceneTree, so server work executes on the same Godot main thread as the graphical client. FirstPersonHotbarNetworkAdapter sends inventory.select_hotbar as ITEM_COMMAND. CanonicalMultiplayerItemGraphService treats that command as a successful canonical mutation, advances item-graph revision/tick and records replay. M3 dedicated runtime then calls _persist_command_result for every successful item command; with persistence enabled this stages the replay record and synchronously calls _persist_checkpoint before sending the result. Thus changing one selected_hotbar_index integer can trigger a complete durable recovery checkpoint on the graphical main thread. Fix8 keeps frozen CH9.6 untouched and changes only the FPE research composition. QuaterniusFirstPersonEmbodimentFix8 no longer constructs or calls the hotbar network adapter for 1..0 input. Slot selection is CLIENT_LOCAL_PRESENTATION state: controller.selected_hotbar_index, right-hand viewmodel and persistent hotbar update synchronously from the already installed canonical replica, with zero ITEM_COMMAND and zero durability request. Structural Item Graph contents remain canonical. If a later canonical structural projection carries an older durable selected_hotbar_index, Fix8 accepts all canonical item/container contents but restores the local presentation selection. Concrete item actions remain server-authoritative: accepted M7/CH9 command normalization sends or derives an explicit canonical item_id for drop/place/mount/equipment operations, and the server still validates ownership and mutation legality. This research result recommends moving active-slot selection out of durable Item Graph mutation semantics in a future canonical contract rather than optimizing disk checkpoints around a transient input state. Third-person held-item presentation remains deferred.
